surprises.head: Washington couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Washington usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 4.6% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.8% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Guentzel has a goal and two assists as the Lightning edge the Capitals
paras: Charle-Édouard D'Astous opened the scoring for the Lightning early in the first. Conor Geekie made it 2-0 late in the period, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Justin Sourdif got the Capitals on the board early in the second, and Emil Lilleberg and Vincent Desharnais dropped the gloves midway through the period. Jake Guentzel shut the door with an empty-netter with just over two minutes left. Guentzel finished with a goal and two assists.

The Lightning had the better of the chances, outshooting the Capitals 30-21 (24-13 at 5-on-5). Andrei Vasilevskiy made 20 saves for the Lightning, and Charlie Lindgren kept the Caps in it, stopping 27 of 29.

Tom Wilson picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Lightning moved to 1-1-0 with a win in their home opener and climbed out of last place in the NHL, while the Capitals dropped to 1-1-0, slipping out of first in the NHL.
